identifiers.title: “You should brush your teeth better”: a randomized controlled trial comparing best-possible versus as-usual toothbrushing
identifiers.authors: Weik U, Shankar-Subramanian S, Sämann T, Wöstmann B, Margraf-Stiksrud J, Deinzer R
identifiers.citation: Weik U, Shankar-Subramanian S, Sämann T, Wöstmann B, Margraf-Stiksrud J, Deinzer R. “You should brush your teeth better”: a randomized controlled trial comparing best-possible versus as-usual toothbrushing. BMC Oral Health. 2023;23. doi:10.1186/s12903-023-03127-3

design.quote: Participants were randomized to one out of two conditions, differing with respect to the instruction they received prior to tooth brushing.

species.quote: Finally, 111 participants were recruited and randomized to the study arms (see Fig. 1).

facts.label: Trial registry entry
facts.quote: This randomized controlled study has been registered at the German Clinical Trials Register (www.drks.de; ID: DRKS00017812; 2019).

facts.label: The trial was registered only after the data were collected
facts.value: retrospectively in August 2019 after completion of data assessment
facts.quote: Registration was conducted retrospectively in August 2019 after completion of data assessment.

facts.label: When the appointments took place
facts.quote: All participants provided informed written consent and were scheduled two different appointments between April 2019 and July 2019.

facts.label: This paper reports only the first of the study's two aims
facts.value: The data presented here refer to the first objective
facts.quote: The data presented here refer to the first objective.

facts.label: How participants were recruited
facts.quote: Study participants were recruited via an internal mailing list of the Justus-Liebig-University Giessen and via online announcements of a regional newspaper.

facts.label: Who could join: students of Giessen aged 18 to 35
facts.value: aged at least 18 to a maximum of 35 years
facts.quote: Inclusion criteria were being a student-resident of Giessen aged at least 18 to a maximum of 35 years as well as the predominant use of a manual toothbrush for at least six months (at least two-thirds of all tooth brushing events).

facts.label: Who could join: mainly used a manual toothbrush
facts.value: predominant use of a manual toothbrush for at least six months
facts.quote: Inclusion criteria were being a student-resident of Giessen aged at least 18 to a maximum of 35 years as well as the predominant use of a manual toothbrush for at least six months (at least two-thirds of all tooth brushing events).

facts.label: Who was excluded (braces, dentures, piercings, recent cleaning, dental or medical training)
facts.value: any training in a dental or medical profession
facts.quote: Exclusion criteria were fixed orthodontic appliances, removable prostheses/dentures, oral piercings or dental jewelry, dental prophylaxis within the previous four months, pregnancy/lactation or use of antibiotics within the previous three months, and any training in a dental or medical profession.

facts.label: Planned sample size
facts.quote: Sample size was calculated using G*Power 3, a free available power analysis program [], and resulted in n = 102 participants needed to detect medium effect sizes (Cohen`s d = 0.5–0.8 []) with α = 5% and test-power of 1–β = 0.80.

facts.label: Number randomized
facts.quote: Finally, 111 participants were recruited and randomized to the study arms (see Fig. 1).

facts.label: Payment to participants
facts.quote: All participants received a monetary compensation of 30 Euros.

facts.label: No tooth cleaning beforehand
facts.quote: All participants were instructed to refrain from any oral hygiene behavior at least four hours before the appointments.

facts.label: Two visits, two weeks apart
facts.value: two appointments that were two weeks apart
facts.quote: Eligible students were scheduled for two appointments that were two weeks apart.

facts.label: Plaque after brushing was measured at the second visit only
facts.value: plaque after brushing was only assessed at the second appointment
facts.quote: While study participants were asked to brush their teeth at both appointments, plaque after brushing was only assessed at the second appointment.

facts.label: Brushing was filmed through a tablet that also served as the mirror
facts.value: served both as a mirror and as a recording tool
facts.quote: This front camera served both as a mirror and as a recording tool for video recording of the participants’ tooth brushing performance.

facts.label: Participants could not see the plaque dye while brushing
facts.quote: A red transparent sheet covered the surface of the tablet display to make plaque staining invisible for the participant.

facts.label: Everyone used the same manual toothbrush and toothpaste
facts.quote: The participants were provided with a standard manual toothbrush (Elmex InterX short brush-head, medium; GABA, Loerrach, Germany) and toothpaste (Elmex; GABA, Loerrach, Germany).

facts.label: Floss and interdental brushes were set out on a table
facts.value: provided on a table beneath the basin
facts.quote: Additionally, dental floss (waxed and unwaxed dental floss; Elmex; GABA, Loerrach, Germany), super floss (Meridol Special-Floss; GABA, Loerrach, Germany) and interdental brushes (Elmex interdental brush sizes 2 and 4; GABA, Loerrach, Germany) were provided on a table beneath the basin.

facts.label: Floss and interdental brushes were on the table for everyone
facts.quote: A2 informed the participants that these devices were at their free disposal.

facts.label: The best-effort instruction
facts.value: brush your teeth as thoroughly as you can so that they are completely clean
facts.quote: These were either “brush your teeth as thoroughly as you can so that they are completely clean” (arm 1; best of one’s abilities (BP)) or “brush your teeth as usual” “(arm 2; as usual (AU)) (instructions are translated from German; for original German instructions, see Appendix).

facts.label: The as-usual instruction
facts.quote: These were either “brush your teeth as thoroughly as you can so that they are completely clean” (arm 1; best of one’s abilities (BP)) or “brush your teeth as usual” “(arm 2; as usual (AU)) (instructions are translated from German; for original German instructions, see Appendix).

facts.label: How the instruction was assigned
facts.quote: For randomization, A2 drew a lot with the respective instruction out of an opaque box.

facts.label: The dentists did not know which instruction a person got
facts.quote: A2 was kept blind regarding the results of the dental examinations, as were the dentists regarding the experimental condition of the participant.

facts.label: Lots split by sex and examining dentist
facts.quote: To stratify with respect to participants’ sex and the examining dentist, lots were distributed to four boxes (one box for each dentist and each sex).

facts.label: Video coders did not know the instruction
facts.value: All examiners were blinded to the experimental conditions
facts.quote: All examiners were blinded to the experimental conditions.

facts.label: Video coders were trained to agree
facts.quote: Calibration was considered successful if an intraclass correlation (ICC) of r ≥ 0.90 was achieved with respect to all behavioral parameters of tooth brushing and interdental hygiene.

facts.label: Plaque measured before and right after brushing
facts.quote: Dental plaque was assessed twice (before and immediately after brushing).

facts.label: Plaque made visible with a dye
facts.quote: Prior to each plaque assessment, dentists dried the teeth with an air stream and applied a plaque disclosing agent (Mira-2-Ton; Hager & Werken, Duisburg, Germany).

facts.label: How gumline plaque was scored: four sections per tooth surface
facts.value: divides the gum line into four equal sections per surface
facts.quote: The MPI divides the gum line into four equal sections per surface (i.e., disto-proximal, disto-cervical, mesio-cervical, mesio-proximal) and assesses the presence (score 1) or absence (score 0) of plaque within each of these sections.

facts.label: The gumline plaque score is the share of sections with plaque
facts.value: The overall MPI is the percentage of positive sections within all sections
facts.quote: The overall MPI is the percentage of positive sections within all sections.

facts.label: A second score: how far plaque spreads up the tooth
facts.value: assesses the extension of plaque throughout the tooth surface
facts.quote: The TQHI assesses the extension of plaque throughout the tooth surface.

facts.label: How perceived cleanliness was rated: a 0 to 100 slider
facts.value: ranging from no cleanliness at all (score 0) to full cleanliness (score 100)
facts.quote: Subjective perception of cleanliness is assessed by a visual analog scale (VAS) presented online ranging from no cleanliness at all (score 0) to full cleanliness (score 100).

facts.label: Before rating, participants learned a dentist's standard of clean
facts.value: a clean surface is only achieved when all plaque deposits, including those at the gum line, are removed
facts.quote: They learned that, in dental judgment, a clean surface is only achieved when all plaque deposits, including those at the gum line, are removed.

facts.label: Main behaviour outcomes
facts.value: tooth contact time and time at occlusal and outer surfaces
facts.quote: The primary outcomes of research Hypothesis a) (brushing to the best of one’s abilities will lead to a different performance) were tooth contact time and time at occlusal and outer surfaces.

facts.label: Main cleanliness outcome: gumline plaque
facts.quote: The primary outcome of research Hypothesis b) (brushing to the best of one’s abilities will lead to a higher degree of achieved oral cleanliness) was the overall MPI.

facts.label: Main perception outcome
facts.quote: The primary outcome of research Hypothesis c) (brushing to the best of one’s abilities will lead to a higher subjectively perceived oral cleanliness) was the overall SPOCd score.

facts.label: People with extreme behaviour values were left out of the analysis
facts.value: three standard deviations from the mean
facts.quote: Participants showing outlying values (defined as three standard deviations from the mean) in any of the behavioral parameters were excluded from final analyses to avoid distorted data.

facts.label: Correction for testing several main outcomes
facts.quote: Bonferroni’s correction was applied for multiple tests within primary outcomes.

facts.label: Some tests were one-tailed
facts.quote: One- and two-tailed tests were applied depending on whether the hypothesis was directed or undirected.

facts.label: Number who finished
facts.quote: One hundred and six participants finished the study (see Fig. 1).

facts.label: Number left out for extreme values
facts.quote: Due to outlying value(s) (M ± 3 SD) in at least one of the behavioral parameters, 15 participants were excluded from statistical analyses.

facts.label: The two groups were alike at the start
facts.value: Groups did not differ with respect to any of these parameters
facts.quote: Groups did not differ with respect to any of these parameters (see Table 1).

facts.label: One perception rating lost
facts.value: Data from one study participant are missing
facts.quote: Data from one study participant are missing due to temporary internet failure.

facts.label: More decayed, missing or filled teeth in the as-usual group
facts.value: a higher DMFT value in the AU group
facts.quote: Descriptive data of the DMFT show differences between the two groups, with a higher DMFT value in the AU group (Table 1).

facts.label: What the final sample could detect
facts.quote: Sensitivity analyses revealed that with the current sample size, an effect size of d = 0.52 (instead of d = 0.50) would be detectable with α = 5% and a power of 1-β = 0.80 [].

facts.label: Analysed group sizes: as usual 45, best effort 46
facts.quote: Brushing as usual (N = 45) | Brushing to the best of one’s ability (N = 46) | p |

The best-effort group brushed longer
facts.quote: Participants in the BP group brushed their teeth longer (p = 0.008, d = 0.57) and used interdental devices more often (p < 0.001).
facts.outcome: Total brushing time

facts.label: The best-effort group brushed longer in total
facts.quote: Analysis of the primary behavioral variables, i.e., total tooth contact time and tooth contact time at the occlusal and outer surfaces, revealed significant group differences in the total tooth contact time (t89 = -2.700; p = 0.008; d = -0.57) and tooth contact time at the outer surfaces (t89 = -3.026; p = 0.003; d = -0.64).
facts.outcome: Total time the brush touched the teeth

facts.label: The best-effort group spent longer on the outer surfaces
facts.quote: Analysis of the primary behavioral variables, i.e., total tooth contact time and tooth contact time at the occlusal and outer surfaces, revealed significant group differences in the total tooth contact time (t89 = -2.700; p = 0.008; d = -0.57) and tooth contact time at the outer surfaces (t89 = -3.026; p = 0.003; d = -0.64).
facts.outcome: Brushing time on the outer (cheek-side) surfaces

facts.label: Best-effort brushing lasted nearly a minute longer

facts.label: More people in the best-effort group used floss or an interdental brush
facts.quote: In total, n = 43 used interdental hygiene devices, with significantly more persons in the BP group than in the AU group (n = 31 vs. n = 12; exact p < 0.001).

facts.quote: The majority of them (n = 38) applied dental floss, whereas only two of the AU group and three of the BP group applied interdental brushes.

facts.label: No clear difference in how many gaps were cleaned

facts.outcome: Number of gaps between teeth cleaned

facts.label: Only four people in each group flossed correctly

facts.outcome: Plaque left along the gumline after brushing (marginal plaque index)

facts.label: How common gum disease is
facts.value: More than 50% of adults are affected
facts.quote: More than 50% of adults are affected by these chronic inflammatory disorders [], and the global prevalence of severe periodontitis is estimated to be eleven to thirteen percent [, ].

facts.label: Plaque left at the gumline is a cause of gum disease
facts.quote: One important etiological factor is persistent marginal plaque [, ].

facts.label: Earlier work compared two groups of 18-year-olds three years apart
facts.value: two cohorts of 18-year-olds examined three years apart
facts.quote: As a first approach to answering this question, Deinzer et al. [] compared the brushing behavior of two cohorts of 18-year-olds examined three years apart.

facts.label: In that earlier work, side-to-side scrubbing was common
facts.value: 40% of the brushing time of lateral surfaces
facts.quote: Furthermore, contrary to current advice, horizontal brushing was very common in both groups (40% of the brushing time of lateral surfaces).

facts.label: Authors' explanation: people brush to remove plaque others can see
facts.quote: This might be due to an important social motive of tooth brushing, i.e., removing visible plaque.

facts.label: No strong evidence that any one brushing movement is better
facts.value: strong evidence proving the superiority of specific movements is missing
facts.quote: While strong evidence proving the superiority of specific movements is missing [], it is remarkable that the instruction to optimize one’s brushing did not change behavior toward more elaborate brushing movements.

facts.label: Authors' reading: 'better' meant more time, not better coverage
facts.value: refers mainly to the brushing quantity in terms of time but not to its quality
facts.quote: The participants’ concept of optimized tooth brushing apparently refers mainly to the brushing quantity in terms of time but not to its quality in terms of sufficient consideration of all surfaces or the application of more elaborate brushing movements.

facts.label: The toothbrush design is unlikely to explain the leftover plaque
facts.value: cannot readily be attributed to an insufficient design of the toothbrush
facts.quote: Therefore, the high levels of remaining plaque cannot readily be attributed to an insufficient design of the toothbrush.

facts.label: Earlier studies: plaque stays at most of the gumline even after best-possible cleaning
facts.value: plaque would persist on most of the marginal areas
facts.quote: Furthermore, the data correspond to those of earlier studies showing that even after the best possible oral hygiene, plaque would persist on most of the marginal areas [, , , , ].

facts.label: Both groups seemed to know their inner surfaces were less clean
facts.value: both groups seem to be aware that they brush their inner surfaces less clean than their outer surfaces
facts.quote: Interestingly, both groups seem to be aware that they brush their inner surfaces less clean than their outer surfaces.

facts.label: Dental professionals asked to brush their best reach almost perfect cleanliness
facts.quote: For dental professionals, this request leads to almost perfect oral cleanliness [].

facts.label: People are not aware of the gap
facts.value: they are not aware of this deficiency
facts.quote: However, they are not aware of this deficiency, as the current data show.

facts.label: Authors' suggestion: teach what to clean, and show people what they miss
facts.quote: Emphasizing the qualitative aspects of tooth brushing behavior and raising awareness of hygiene deficits could be a first step toward improving the effectiveness of oral hygiene.

facts.label: Clinically, the plaque differences were small
facts.quote: Nonetheless, from a clinical point of view, the differences were still small, and the overall oral cleanliness was far below what is achievable by appropriately trained people.

facts.label: The differences that were not clear were far smaller than the study could detect
facts.value: all nonsignificant effect sizes were far below the level that could have been significant
facts.quote: In addition, all nonsignificant effect sizes were far below the level that could have been significant with the targeted sample size.

facts.label: Only university students were studied
facts.quote: First, the participants were university students, and thus the data might not transfer to other populations.

facts.label: One brushing session only
facts.quote: Second, the results focus on only one toothbrushing event.

facts.label: Unknown what longer-term extra effort would do
facts.value: No information is available on how oral hygiene would improve
facts.quote: No information is available on how oral hygiene would improve if people would increase their efforts for a longer period.
